name: a small patch of alligator cracking — a net of three or four small polygons outlined by dark grey-black cracks, one plate slightly lifted, drawn as a transparent decal on old asphalt
label: wasteland_ruins/road-crack-c
reasons: 화풍: 칸 정보량이 기준보다 훨씬 낮음 (4/4)

refSet.reason: 칩셋 wasteland_ruins 의 화풍 기준 묶음이 없다

surfaces.part: alligator crack net decal (polygons outlined by dark cracks, one lifted plate)

answer.evidence: The object is a transparent floor decal of dark crack lines (rows 3-13) seen from above, with a few brownish and grey highlight pixels for the lifted plate. The silhouette is sparse and irregular (widths 2-9 px) with no solid face, no front-edge line, no eave shadow, and no vertical front face. That is the expected appearance for a flat decal, so it reads as a top-down slab with no front face.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate renders as a tiny glyph, much smaller than the 4x3-tile patch it should cover, and it sits on a dark backdrop. The measured tone counts are 0 because it is smaller than one tile, so I judged by eye. It uses only 4 distinct colours in total, against 80 for the grass reference and 7 for the paving reference. That gives about 3 shading steps, with no visible plate lift, no per-plate shading, no asphalt grain and no speckle. Compared with the paving reference (about 7 visible tones, with stones shaded one by one and per-slab highlights), it is much thinner and reads as a flat sticker. The dark-edge neutral share is 4%, so the cracks lean slightly tinted rather than pure black, but at this size the outline treatment barely matters. The piece is sparse, but a careful artist would not accept it next to the references. It is far less rich and does not fill the intended 4x3 area.

surfaces.part: alligator crack net decal (polygons outlined by dark cracks, one lifted plate)

answer.evidence: The decal is a sparse net of dark grey-black crack lines (rows 3-13, widths 2-9 px) on a transparent ground. It is seen straight from above as a flat pattern. There is no front face, no front-edge line, no eave shadow and no ellipse, and no vertical south face of 3 or more rows. The lifted plate is only a few lighter and brown pixels at rows 6-9 and 13 and does not form a vertical face. For a flat kind this is a flat top-down plate with no front face, so top_down_slab.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a tiny decal, smaller than one 16x16 tile, so the per-tile facts read 0 and I judged by eye. It has only 4 distinct colours in total. The reference grass has 80 and the paving 7 per tile, with about 3 and 7 visible tones. The candidate's material ramp has about 3 steps: a mid asphalt tone, a dark crack line and one lighter lifted-plate edge, against about 5-6 in the references. Only 4% of its dark edge pixels are neutral, so the crack lines carry a slight tint rather than being pure black. That does not offset the shallow ramp. The decal has no grain, speckle or per-plate shading, and it reads as a thin sticker-like glyph next to the richly textured grass and paving. It also does not give a 4x3-tile ground patch the density of the references.

surfaces.part: alligator crack net decal on asphalt (flat polygons outlined by dark cracks)

The width profile shows irregular crack lines (widths 2-9) and not a body with a front face. It is seen from above as a flat plate, which matches the flat kind. The lifted plate is only a slight lighter patch, not a front face of 3 or more rows.

The cracks read as a uniform dark grey line on every shape, which is the sticker look. The near-neutral dark-edge share of 4% is not evidence of a tinted outline; with so few pixels the measurement is unreliable, so I judge by eye.
